items.desc: Iraq has agreed with the US to allow oil exports through Hormuz, minister says Iraq has reached understandings with the US to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an interview with Al Jazeera. items.title: Iran says no progress on US negotiations since midterm results
items.desc: Iran says no progress on US negotiations since midterm results Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that there has been no progress in mediators' work regarding peace talks between Tehran and Washington to end hostilities in the region since the results of the US midterm elections. “The main reason is the US election results, which have obviously come as a shock to everyone,” Araghchi told reporters. “It will take some time for things to settle down and for the atmosphere to become conducive to the mediators resuming their visits. We have to wait,” he added.

items.desc: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Monday he had directed the foreign ministry to pursue all possible means to urgently “escalate humanitarian assistance” to Gaza, where heavy rains have flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians. items.desc: LAHORE: Lahore was ranked the world’s most polluted major city on Monday as its Air Quality Index (AQI) reached 590, according to IQAir. A separate historical reading on the platform, however, showed an hourly index of 647, placing the city in the hazardous category. items.desc: LAHORE: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has increased the limit of personal loans available under the Youth Business and Agriculture Loan schemes, and reduced the minimum age limit to allow 18-year-olds to avail the scheme as well. items.desc: LAHORE: The historical Gurdwara Chhevin Patshahi Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib on Temple Road, Mozang, which had been closed since the Partition, was reopened here on Sunday after completion of its restoration. items.title: Bangladesh's external debt increases almost threefold in decade
items.desc: Bangladesh’s foreign debt has almost tripled in 10 years, a steeper rise than in any other South Asian country except the Maldives, according to the World Bank. Even so, the country has a lower debt burden relative to export earnings than Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bhutan. However, its burden is higher than that of India and Nepal. According to the World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026, Bangladesh’s total foreign debt stood at $113 billion at the end of 2025, up from about $38 billion in 2015. items.desc: Visiting Srinagar once, Indian essayist Pankaj Mishra found Iqbal in a rather unexpected place. Or, at least, in an unlikely heart. items.desc: PAKISTAN’S 2024 election results marked the end of a political cycle that began in the early 2000s.
